claim.pdf_says: 14.9.46.2 General format:  TERMINATE { report-name-1 } …   - with TERMINATE underlined (confirmed on a 300 dpi crop: a continuous rule runs under the whole word); report-name-1 is not underlined.
claim.markdown_says: TERMINATE { report-name-1 } …   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 32275) - no <u> markup, no figure note.
claim.why_it_matters: The underline marks TERMINATE as a required word (5.2.6.2). The immediately preceding statement in the same file preserves exactly this marking - 14.9.45.2 is transcribed as '<u>SUPPRESS</u> PRINTING' (line 32228) - so the TERMINATE figure has silently lost information its neighbour kept, and a reader or generator consuming the markdown has no way to know TERMINATE is required rather than optional.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED after attempting every available refutation.

(1) PDF glyphs, inspected directly. Rendered page 796 at 300 dpi (2550x3300) and cropped the general-format line (x 230-1050, y 780-890) at 2x. What I see: the word TERMINATE set in roman caps with a single continuous horizontal rule running beneath it, beginning under the left stem of the T and ending under the final E, terminating before the space that precedes the opening brace. '{ report-name-1 }' and the trailing ellipsis carry no rule. The rule's extent matches the word's advance width exactly, so it is a keyword underline, not a table rule, cell border, or hyperlink decoration. The claim's characterization of the PDF is accurate.

(2) The 'missing' markup is genuinely absent, not reflowed or relocated. `grep -n '<u>TERMINATE</u>' specs/ISO_COBOL.md` returns zero hits anywhere in the 52k-line file. The only general-format occurrence is the bare line 32278 'TERMINATE { report-name-1 } …'. The page work unit reports has_figure=false and its markdown slice carries no figure-note block, so the marking is not preserved in prose either. Nothing recovers it.

(3) Not merely formatting - it inverts the meaning. The file states its own convention at line 2631 (5.2.2 Keywords): keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required...'; and at line 2644 (5.2.3 Optional words): optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats... They may be written to add clarity.' TERMINATE therefore appears in the markdown in precisely the typographic form the standard reserves for a word that MAY BE OMITTED. The transcription does not merely drop an ornament, it asserts the opposite of the truth about the only reserved word in the format.

(4) The decisive test - is dropping <u> simply this transcription's house style? No. 156 <u> tags exist file-wide. More pointedly, the structurally IDENTICAL sibling statement is marked correctly: line 27726 reads '<u>INITIATE</u> { report-name-1 } …' - same one-line plain-text format, same brace group, same operand, same ellipsis, underline preserved. The immediately preceding statement, SUPPRESS, is likewise '<u>SUPPRESS</u> PRINTING' at line 32231. (The GENERATE format at 27204 is a fenced code block, a different rendering class where <u> is not used, so it is not a counterexample.) TERMINATE is the lone outlier in its own comparison class - the INITIATE/TERMINATE pair that opens and closes a report. This is a local omission, not a convention.

No refutation available on any axis: the text is absent, the loss is semantic rather than cosmetic, and the file's own sibling entries establish the expected markup.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and the substance is correctly reported, but two citations in the claim are wrong and should be fixed before the finding is filed. CORRECTED LINE NUMBERS. The claim cites the anchor lines rather than the content lines, off by three in both cases. The TERMINATE general format is at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 32278 (32275 is ''). The SUPPRESS comparison is at line 32231 (32228 is ''). CORRECTED CONVENTION CITATION. The underline rule is NOT 5.2.6.2 - that section is 'Brackets' (line 2691) and concerns [ ] optionality. The governing text is 5.2.2 Keywords (line 2631), 'shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword', paired with 5.2.3 Optional words (line 2644), 'shown in uppercase and not underlined... They may be written to add clarity.' STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN THE CLAIM OFFERS. The claim rests its case on the preceding statement, SUPPRESS. The better witness is INITIATE at line 27726, 'INITIATE { report-name-1 } …' - byte-for-byte the same format shape as TERMINATE (one-line plain text, brace-wrapped report-name-1, trailing ellipsis) and the paired statement that opens the report TERMINATE closes. Its underline is preserved. This rules out the main innocent explanation, that this transcription simply does not carry underlines in general formats: 156 tags exist file-wide and the exact structural twin retains its own. SHARPENED IMPACT. Because 5.2.3 assigns a definite meaning to an uppercase word printed WITHOUT an underline, the markdown does not merely omit information - it affirmatively encodes TERMINATE as an optional word that may be omitted from the statement. A grammar or reserved-word generator reading the transcription would derive an omittable verb for the TERMINATE statement. FIX. Change line 32278 to 'TERMINATE { report-name-1 } …' to match INITIATE at 27726 and SUPPRESS at 32231.
